newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-ANGRY REAL FANS HURL INSULTS AT CAPELLO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ANGRY REAL FANS HURL INSULTS AT CAPELLO.

text.p: Angry Real Madrid fans hurled insults and abuse at coach Fabio Capello on Tuesday when he left the training ground soon after announcing he was quitting the club.

Capello, who only joined Real at the start of the season, confirmed earlier on Tuesday that he was leaving the club at the end of the season -- despite the fact they are poised to win the Spanish League title.

His imminent resignation prompted renewed speculation that he will return to struggling Italian champions AC Milan, who he steered to four victories in five seasons as well as the European Cup in 1994.
"I am sure that Real will win the league, and the Champions' League next season," said Capello, whose side are eight points clear of Barcelona.
Tenerife coach Jupp Heynckes is the clear favourite to succeed Capello at the Bernabeu stadium.
Real president Lorenzo Sanz, who had hit out at Capello earlier in the day, called an emergency board meeting for later on Tuesday.
But Sanz quashed rumours that he would try to fire Capello.
"We have little to say, we will be all together until the end of the season, and we will give all the necessary support," said Sanz.
Sanz's words echoed those of his coach earlier in the day.
"The most important thing now is to think of winning the league," said Capello, who toned down criticisms levelled at Sanz in a radio programme early on Tuesday morning.
Capello's decision to read out a statement, rather than hold a press conference, also led commentators to conclude that he had been warned against inflaming the situation.
Angry Real fans shouted insults at Capello as he left the Real training ground while Sanz had attacked Capello in another radio interview early on Tuesday.

"He threatened to work badly to get the contract ended," said Sanz, "Capello negotiated with (Barcelona vice-president Joan) Gaspart, he made fun of us." d brought Capello to Real after a disastrous season in which the six-times European champions had failed to qualify for continental competition for only the second occasion in their illustrious history.
Capello forged a workmanlike outfit whose efficiency contrasted with the stylish anarchy of Bobby Robson's Barcelona.
Capello won over Madrid fans with a 2-0 league victory over Barcelona, but by January there were already rumours of problems with Sanz and the Real board.
Davor Suker and Predrag Mijatovic, both strikers signed by Sanz, are amongst players to have clashed with Capello.

The problems of AC Milan, who crashed out of the Champions' League and are struggling to ensure a UEFA Cup place for next season, increased speculation that Capello would return to Italy to replace Arrigo Sacchi.
Capello is understood to have already laid down guidelines for a new team at Milan.
Argentine midfielder Fernando Redondo and Brazilian left-back Roberto Carlos are rumoured to be amongst Real players on Capello's shopping list.
Ironically Alfonso Perez, the international striker sold off by Real Madrid to Betis in the close season, is another player linked strongly to AC Milan.
